text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- High Court hears opening arguments by Prime Minister's lawyer on why JB Jeyaretnam's seemingly innocuous reference to police reports filed by Tang Liang Hong was defamatory.

- Lawyers acting for Jeyaretnam initiated talks for an out-of-court settlement of defamation suits by People's Action Party leaders against him on Friday, says Lim Siam Kim, press secretary to Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
- Keppel Group and Port of Singapore Authority joining forces to develop adjacent land parcels at massive waterfront sites at Telok Blangah.
- Regional stock markets suffer in wake of thunderous fall in Wall Street last Friday that left sentiment bruised heavily and investor confidence shattered.
- Southeast Asian currencies continue to languish under poor investment sentiment with Indonesian rupiah breaching 3,000 level for first time, peso at new low and ringgit suffering fresh losses.
- Port of Singapore Authority considering mega-cruise centre at four-storey Singapore Port Institute next to World Trade Centre with facilities rivalling Changi Airport.

- ST Aerospace may well have to review issue of Foreign and Local listings if parent company Singapore Technologies were to sell part of its shareholding, says group president and chief executive of ST Aero Boon Swan Foo.
- Singapore Technologies Aerospace reports four-fold rise in first-half earnings from S$6.86 million to S$28 million -- more than what it made for whole of last year.
- ST Electronic & Engineering posts 61.9 percent jump in interim net profit to S$4.8 million, following acquisition of four companies.
- SM Summit Holdings stock plummets to lowest level for year, after marginal rally last Thursday.
- Industrial equipment supplier Ace Dynamics, formerly known as Causeway Investment, back in the black with net earnings of S$546,000 for the half year ended June 30.
- Datacraft Asia Ltd reports 54.8 percent jump in net profits to US$10.3 million for full year ended June, beating analysts' consensus forecasts of 51 percent growth.
- Inno-Pacific Holdings scales down proposed plan announced in June to raise over S$200 million through a rights issue with warrants.
